dedupe_keys.name: egret electrical grid research and engineering tools

description: EGRET is a Python package for electrical grid optimisation built on the Pyomo modelling language. It was first released in 2019 by Sandia National Laboratories, with Bernard Knueven, Carl Laird, Jean-Paul Watson, Michael Bynum and Anya Castillo as primary contributors, to serve both as an engine for solving standard grid optimisation problems and as a flexible base for researchers testing new formulations. Features are unit commitment, economic dispatch and optimal power flow (DC and AC), AC relaxations, PTDF-based formulations, a library of problem formulations and approximations, generic handling of grid data across formulations through a ModelData object, and a declarative model representation. Coverage is not tied to a place. The code is accessible on GitHub under a BSD licence from National Technology and Engineering Solutions of Sandia at no cost, is packaged as gridx-egret, and remains maintained (ten tags, latest commit May 2026). Caveats: solving large models needs a separate mathematical solver, and documentation is mainly in the code. Simulation uses are production cost, unit commitment and optimal power flow studies. Related records: model-powermodels-jl and model-matpower are comparable optimisation tools.
